name: Shuo Liu

papers.title: MolmoAct2: Action Reasoning Models for Real-World Deployment
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models aim to provide a single generalist controller for robots, but today's systems fall short on the criteria that matter for real-world deployment. Frontier models are closed, open-weight alternatives are tied to expensive hardware, reasoning-augmented policies pay prohibitive latency for their grounding, and fine-tuned success rates remain below the threshold for dependable use. We present MolmoAct2, a fully open action reasoning model built for practical deployment, advancing its predecessor, MolmoAct along five axes. We introduce Molmo2-ER, a VLM backbone specialized for spatial and embodied reasoning, trained on a 3.3M-sample corpus with a specialize-then-rehearse recipe. We release three new datasets spanning low-to-medium cost platforms: MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM Dataset, 720 hours of teleoperated bimanual trajectories that constitute the largest open bimanual dataset to date; MolmoAct2-DROID Dataset, a quality-filtered Franka subset of DROID; and MolmoAct2-SO100/101 Dataset, a quality-filtered SO-100/101 subset. We provide OpenFAST Tokenizer, an open-weight, open-data action tokenizer trained on millions of trajectories across five embodiments. We redesign the architecture to graft a flow-matching continuous-action expert onto a discrete-token VLM via per-layer KV-cache conditioning. Finally, we propose MolmoAct2-Think, an adaptive-depth reasoning variant that re-predicts depth tokens only for scene regions that change between timesteps, retaining geometric grounding at a fraction of prior latency. In the most extensive empirical study of any open VLA to date, spanning 7 simulation and real-world benchmarks, MolmoAct2 outperforms strong baselines including π0.5, while Molmo2-ER surpasses GPT-5 and Gemini Robotics ER-1.5 across 13 embodied-reasoning benchmarks. We release model weights, training code, and complete training data.

papers.title: VLS: Steering Pretrained Robot Policies via Vision–Language Models
papers.abstract: Why do pretrained diffusion or flow-matching policies fail when the same task is performed under ambiguous instructions or slightly complex scenarios? Such failures rarely reflect missing motor skills; instead, they exposea limitation of imitation learning under train–test shifts, where action generation is tightly coupled to training-specific semantic and spatial context. To address this, we propose Vision–Language Steering (VLS), a training-free framework for inference-time adaptation of frozen generative robot policies. VLS treats adaptation as an inference-time control problem, steering the sampling process in response to out-of-distribution observation–language inputs without modifying policy parameters. By leveraging vision–language models to synthesize programmatic, trajectory-differentiable reward functions over grounded 3D keypoints, VLS guides denoising toward action trajectories satisfying test-time spatial and task requirements. In simulation and real-world evaluations, VLS outperforms prior steering methods, with up to 9.6×gain over the base policy on CALVIN, +13 pts over the same frozen π0.5 on LIBERO-PRO, and +4.3 pts on average over the strongest VLM-verifier baseline on LIBERO-10-R. Real-world deployment further demonstrates robust adaptation under spatial and semantic shifts.
